title: Caching Layers Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on where caches sit (client, CDN, app, database), the read/write patterns, eviction, invalidation and thundering herd, ending with a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Cache Layers Mental Model
points: Cache = small fast copy of slow data; a hit skips the origin, a miss pays full cost then fills the cache; hit ratio = hits / (hits + misses)
Client layer: browser/HTTP cache driven by Cache-Control (max-age, no-store, no-cache, private) and ETag/If-None-Match revalidation (304)
CDN layer: edge servers cache static and public responses near users; controlled by s-maxage and Vary; cuts latency and origin load
App layer: in-process cache (fast, per-instance, inconsistent across servers) vs distributed cache like Redis/Memcached (shared, one network hop)
Database layer: buffer pool/query cache inside the DB; closest to data, last line of defense; each layer outward is faster but staler

chapters.title: Read and Write Caching Patterns
points: Cache-aside (lazy loading): app reads cache, on miss reads DB, then writes cache; app owns the logic; only requested data is cached; most common pattern
Write-through: write goes to cache and DB synchronously; cache never stale for written keys; slower writes, may cache data never read
Write-back (write-behind): write to cache, flush to DB asynchronously in batches; fastest writes, but data lost if cache dies before flush
Write-around: write straight to DB, skip cache; avoids polluting cache with write-once data; next read is a miss
Pseudo-code cache-aside: v = cache.get(k); if v is None: v = db.get(k); cache.set(k, v, ttl=300); return v

chapters.title: Eviction Policies
points: Eviction runs when the cache is full to free space; policy decides the victim
LRU: evict the least recently used entry; O(1) with hash map + doubly linked list; default choice for recency-skewed workloads
LFU: evict the least frequently used; protects hot keys; weak against old once-popular keys, needs frequency aging
TTL: entry expires after a fixed time regardless of space; bounds staleness; not a space-management policy by itself, so combine with LRU/LFU
Redis example: maxmemory 2gb with maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru; volatile-* policies only evict keys that have a TTL; noeviction returns write errors when full

chapters.title: Invalidation Strategies
points: Invalidation is deciding when a cached copy is no longer valid; the hardest part of caching
TTL expiry: simplest, tolerates bounded staleness; choose TTL from how stale the data may be
Explicit invalidation: delete the key on write (DB update, then cache.delete); prefer delete over set to avoid racing writers storing stale values
Versioned keys or URLs (user:42:v7, app.3f9a.js): new version is a new key, so no purge needed; ideal for CDN and client assets
CDN purge by URL or tag/surrogate key; propagation is not instant, so pair with short s-maxage for dynamic content

chapters.title: Thundering Herd and Common Mistakes
points: Thundering herd (cache stampede): a hot key expires, many requests miss at once and all hit the DB together
Fix with request coalescing: a per-key lock or single-flight so one request rebuilds while others wait or serve stale
Fix with TTL jitter (ttl = base + random) so keys do not expire in the same instant; also pre-warm or refresh early before expiry
Cache penetration: repeated misses for keys that do not exist bypass the cache; cache a null with short TTL or use a Bloom filter
Mistake: caching without a TTL or eviction limit, so stale data and memory grow forever; also caching per-user data in a shared CDN without Vary or private

chapters.title: Caching Cheat Sheet
points: Layers outward to inward: client, CDN, app (local or Redis), database; cache as close to the user as correctness allows
Pattern pick: cache-aside for read-heavy default; write-through for consistency; write-back for write throughput accepting loss risk
Eviction pick: LRU default, LFU for stable hot sets, TTL always to bound staleness
Invalidation pick: TTL plus delete-on-write; version keys for static assets
Stampede defense: single-flight lock, TTL jitter, serve stale while revalidating, null caching for missing keys
